theme: Talking about what you can do — the potential form
intro: Turn plain verbs into can-do verbs, and learn the one particle that quietly changes when you do.

grammar.title: The potential form (可能形)

rules.label: る-verbs (ichidan)
rules.detail: drop る, add られる
examples: 食べる → 食べられる (can eat)
見る → 見られる (can see/watch)

rules.label: Irregulars
examples: 来る → 来られる／こられる (can come)

grammar.bigPoint: With the potential form the object usually takes が instead of を: 日本語を話す → 日本語が話せる.

vocab.en: to speak → 話せる can speak
to read → 読める can read
to swim → 泳げる can swim
to reserve → 予約できる can reserve

examples.jp: 私は日本語がすこし話せます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa nihongo ga sukoshi hanasemasu.
examples.en: I can speak a little Japanese.

examples.jp: 辛いものが食べられますか。

note: Once a verb is in the potential form it behaves like a る-verb, so conjugate onward normally: 話せます, 話せない, 話せて. Use できる wherever you'd want the potential of する (オンラインで予約できます). Keep the を → が shift in mind — it's the tell a native ear expects.

selfCheck.q: Using 読む, how do you say "I can read hiragana"?
selfCheck.a: ひらがなが読めます。(Hiragana ga yomemasu.)
